content:
This past July, Apple rolled out a basic search feature update for its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be widely praised, but the same version of TestFlight also introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't too affected by this bug. So I see this TestFlight update as a small but meaningful step forward.

Sometimes a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of beta testing apps installed — Apple's latest TestFlight update is a clear example. Apple has just updated TestFlight across multiple platforms such as iPhone, iPad, and Mac. The new version 4.3 adds a "search bar for quickly finding apps".

Looking back, I did notice some unusual situations at the time and noted them at the end of my article (although my judgment then was completely the opposite):

The reason I didn't treat this as a bug is that when I merged my two separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts last year, I retained TestFlight app records I had accumulated over the years. The process wasn't exactly convenient, but I felt it was worth it.

In any case, the TestFlight bug wasn't ignored — John Vorhees of MacStories discovered it:

So when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac mentioning that TestFlight had finally added a search bar, you can imagine how excited I was. I thought: "Finally!" and immediately dropped what I was doing to update the app. [...] But there's a big "however" to this. Previously, TestFlight's beta tests were arranged in reverse chronological order, which is exactly the way I liked it. [...] Now, expired betas and still-active betas are all jumbled together, sorted alphabetically, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I did a rough count — for me, there are nearly 800 app records. As you'd expect, very few of these betas are actually useful. The search function does help, but you can no longer scroll through them one by one.

Later in August, John Gruber wrote an article on Daring Fireball about the TestFlight update and the bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was noted by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the update notes only mention bug fixes, this update does indeed address the bug in question.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is precisely the fix provided for users affected by this regression issue.
